question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{5}{2\sqrt[3]{x}}-3
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{5}{2\sqrt[3]{y}}-3.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{5}{2\sqrt[3]{y}}-3 \\ \frac{5}{2\sqrt[3]{y}} & =x+3 \\ \sqrt[3]{y} & =\frac{5}{2(x+3)} \\ {(\sqrt[3]{y})}^{3} & ={(\frac{5}{2(x+3)})}^{3} \\ y & =\frac{125}{8(x+3)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{125}{8(x+3)^{3}}.
$$

**Note**: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are

$$
x\ne 0,\,f(x)\ne -3.
$$

Therefore, the domain and range of ${f}^{-1}(x)$ are

$$
x\ne -3,\,{f}^{-1}(x)\ne 0.
$$
